test_cases.description: Registration with a fresh email returns a user, a JWT and its TTL
steps: POST /api/auth/register with body {"email":"ada@example.com","password":"correct-horse","display_name":"Ada"}
test_cases.expected: 201 Created; body has user.id (string), user.email == "ada@example.com", user.display_name == "Ada", a non-empty token string and expires_in == 86400; no password or password_hash field appears anywhere in the response; a users document exists with email "ada@example.com"

test_cases.description: Registering an email that already exists returns 409, compared case-insensitively
steps: POST /api/auth/register with {"email":"dup@example.com","password":"correct-horse"}
POST /api/auth/register again with {"email":"DUP@Example.COM","password":"another-password-9"}
test_cases.expected: First call 201. Second call 409 Conflict with error == "email_already_registered" and no token in the body; the users collection still contains exactly one document for dup@example.com and its password_hash is unchanged from the first registration

test_cases.description: Registration rejects a password shorter than the 8-character minimum
steps: POST /api/auth/register with {"email":"short@example.com","password":"abc123"}
test_cases.expected: 422 Unprocessable Entity with error == "unprocessable_entity" and details containing an entry whose field == "password"; no users document is created for short@example.com

test_cases.description: Registration rejects a missing or malformed email address
steps: POST /api/auth/register with {"password":"correct-horse"} (no email key)
POST /api/auth/register with {"email":"not-an-email","password":"correct-horse"}
test_cases.expected: Both calls return 422 with details containing an entry whose field == "email"; no user documents are created by either call

test_cases.description: A registered password is stored as a bcrypt hash, never in plaintext
steps: POST /api/auth/register with {"email":"hash@example.com","password":"correct-horse"}
Read the users document for hash@example.com from MongoDB
test_cases.expected: 201 Created; the stored document has no `password` field, and password_hash is a bcrypt string starting with "$2" and containing the cost segment "$12$" — it is not equal to "correct-horse"

test_cases.description: Login with correct credentials returns a usable token
steps: POST /api/auth/register with {"email":"login@example.com","password":"correct-horse"}
POST /api/auth/login with {"email":"LOGIN@example.com","password":"correct-horse"}
test_cases.expected: 200 OK; body has user.id equal to the id returned at registration, user.email == "login@example.com", a token string and expires_in == 86400; using that token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on GET /api/notes returns 200

test_cases.description: Login with a wrong password returns 401 with no token
steps: POST /api/auth/register with {"email":"probe@example.com","password":"correct-horse"}
POST /api/auth/login with {"email":"probe@example.com","password":"wrong-password-1"}
test_cases.expected: 401 Unauthorized with error == "invalid_credentials" and message == "Email or password is incorrect."; no token field in the response body

test_cases.description: Login with an unknown email returns a response byte-identical to the wrong-password response, so accounts cannot be probed
steps: POST /api/auth/login with {"email":"probe@example.com","password":"wrong-password-1"} (existing user, wrong password)
POST /api/auth/login with {"email":"nobody-here@example.com","password":"wrong-password-1"} (no such user)
test_cases.expected: Both return 401 and their JSON bodies are identical (same error code and same message string) — nothing in status, error, or message distinguishes an unknown email from a wrong password

test_cases.description: Login rejects a request missing required fields with 422 rather than 401
steps: POST /api/auth/login with {"email":"login@example.com"} (no password key)
test_cases.expected: 422 Unprocessable Entity with error == "unprocessable_entity" and details containing an entry whose field == "password"; no token is issued

test_cases.description: Creating a note with a valid token returns the persisted note
steps: POST /api/notes with header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and body {"title":"Groceries","body":"milk, eggs"}
test_cases.expected: 201 Created; body has a string id, title == "Groceries", body == "milk, eggs", ISO8601 created_at and updated_at; the stored notes document has owner_id equal to the token's user, deleted_at == null, and no owner_id is echoed in the response

test_cases.description: Title is optional — a note created without one comes back with title null
steps: POST /api/notes with a valid bearer token and body {"body":"just a body, no title"}
test_cases.expected: 201 Created with title == null (JSON null, not the string "null" and not absent) and body == "just a body, no title"

test_cases.description: Creating a note with no Authorization header is refused before any write
steps: POST /api/notes with NO Authorization header and body {"body":"should never be stored"}
test_cases.expected: 401 Unauthorized with error == "unauthorized"; response contains no note id and no note data; the notes collection gains no document with body "should never be stored"

test_cases.description: A malformed, wrongly-signed, or non-Bearer token is rejected with 401
steps: POST /api/notes with header `Authorization: Bearer not.a.jwt` and body {"body":"x"}
POST /api/notes with header `Authorization: <valid-token>` (Bearer prefix omitted) and body {"body":"x"}
POST /api/notes with a JWT signed with a different secret and body {"body":"x"}
test_cases.expected: All three return 401 with error == "unauthorized" and identical bodies; no notes documents are created

test_cases.description: An expired JWT is rejected on a notes route
steps: POST /api/notes with an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` whose exp claim is in the past (signed with the server's JWT_SECRET) and body {"body":"expired token note"}
test_cases.expected: 401 Unauthorized with error == "unauthorized"; no note is created

test_cases.description: owner_id in the request body is ignored — a client cannot create a note for another user
steps: Register user A and user B; capture A's token and B's user id
POST /api/notes as user A with body {"body":"planted note","owner_id":"<user B id>"}
test_cases.expected: 201 Created; the stored note's owner_id equals user A's id, not user B's; GET /api/notes as user B returns total 0 and no item with body "planted note", while GET /api/notes as user A includes it

test_cases.description: An empty or whitespace-only body is rejected with 422
steps: POST /api/notes with a valid token and body {"body":""}
POST /api/notes with a valid token and body {"body":"     "}
POST /api/notes with a valid token and body {"title":"only a title"} (no body key)
test_cases.expected: All three return 422 with error == "unprocessable_entity" and details containing an entry whose field == "body"; the notes collection gains no documents from these calls

test_cases.description: Body length boundary: 10,000 characters is accepted, 10,001 is rejected
steps: POST /api/notes with a valid token and body {"body":"<exactly 10000 'a' characters>"}
POST /api/notes with a valid token and body {"body":"<exactly 10001 'a' characters>"}
test_cases.expected: First call 201 Created with a body field of length 10000. Second call 422 with details field == "body"; no second note is stored

test_cases.description: Body is trimmed before storage and length is measured after trimming
steps: POST /api/notes with a valid token and body {"body":"   padded note   "}
test_cases.expected: 201 Created with body == "padded note" (no leading or trailing whitespace) in both the response and the stored document

test_cases.description: A title longer than 200 characters is rejected with 422
steps: POST /api/notes with a valid token and body {"title":"<201 'a' characters>","body":"valid body"}
test_cases.expected: 422 Unprocessable Entity with details containing an entry whose field == "title"; no note is created

test_cases.description: Listing returns the caller's notes newest-first with default paging metadata
steps: As one user, POST /api/notes three times with bodies "first", "second", "third" (in that order)
GET /api/notes with that user's bearer token and no query parameters
test_cases.expected: 200 OK with page == 1, limit == 20, total == 3, and items[].body == ["third","second","first"] — created_at descending

test_cases.description: List returns only the caller's notes, never another user's
steps: Register users A and B; as A POST /api/notes with body "A-note"; as B POST /api/notes with body "B-note"
GET /api/notes with A's bearer token
GET /api/notes with B's bearer token
test_cases.expected: A's response is 200 with total == 1 and the only item's body == "A-note"; B's response is 200 with total == 1 and body == "B-note"; neither response contains the other user's note

test_cases.description: Soft-deleted notes are excluded from list responses and from the total count
steps: As one user, create two notes; capture id1 and id2
DELETE /api/notes/<id1> with that user's token
GET /api/notes with the same token
test_cases.expected: 200 OK with total == 1 and items containing only id2; id1 appears in no item; the id1 document still exists in MongoDB with a non-null deleted_at

test_cases.description: Listing without a valid token returns 401 and leaks no note data
steps: GET /api/notes with no Authorization header
GET /api/notes with header `Authorization: Bearer garbage`
test_cases.expected: Both return 401 with error == "unauthorized"; neither response body contains an `items`, `total`, or any note field

test_cases.description: Page size above the 100 cap is rejected with 422 rather than silently clamped
steps: GET /api/notes?limit=101 with a valid bearer token
test_cases.expected: 422 Unprocessable Entity with error == "unprocessable_entity" and details containing an entry whose field == "limit"; no items array is returned

test_cases.description: limit=100 (the boundary) is accepted
steps: GET /api/notes?limit=100&page=1 with a valid bearer token
test_cases.expected: 200 OK with limit == 100 and page == 1 in the response body

test_cases.description: Non-integer or out-of-range paging parameters return 422
steps: GET /api/notes?page=abc with a valid bearer token
GET /api/notes?page=0 with a valid bearer token
GET /api/notes?limit=-5 with a valid bearer token
test_cases.expected: All three return 422 with details naming the offending field ("page" or "limit"); no items array is returned

test_cases.description: Pagination pages correctly through more notes than one page holds
steps: As one user, create 25 notes with bodies "note-01" … "note-25" in ascending order
GET /api/notes?page=1 with that user's token
GET /api/notes?page=2 with that user's token
test_cases.expected: Page 1: 200 with total == 25, limit == 20, items.length == 20, first item body == "note-25". Page 2: 200 with total == 25, page == 2, items.length == 5, first item body == "note-05"; the two pages share no ids

test_cases.description: Fetching one of the caller's own notes by id returns it
steps: POST /api/notes with a valid token and body {"title":"T","body":"fetch me"}; capture the returned id
GET /api/notes/<id> with the same token
test_cases.expected: 200 OK with id equal to the captured id, title == "T", body == "fetch me", and ISO8601 created_at and updated_at

test_cases.description: Fetching another user's note returns 404, not 403, so ids are not enumerable
steps: As user A, POST /api/notes with body {"body":"A private"}; capture idA
GET /api/notes/<idA> with user B's bearer token
test_cases.expected: 404 Not Found with error == "not_found" (never 403); the response contains no title or body from A's note, and GET /api/notes/<idA> as A still returns 200

test_cases.description: A soft-deleted note is no longer fetchable by id
steps: Create a note as one user and capture its id
DELETE /api/notes/<id> with that user's token
GET /api/notes/<id> with the same token
test_cases.expected: 404 Not Found with error == "not_found"; the underlying document still exists in MongoDB with deleted_at set

test_cases.description: A non-existent or malformed note id is indistinguishable from a forbidden one
steps: GET /api/notes/64b7f0000000000000000000 (well-formed ObjectId that matches no note) with a valid token
GET /api/notes/not-an-objectid with a valid token
test_cases.expected: Both return 404 with identical bodies (error == "not_found"); neither returns 400 or 500, so a malformed id and an unowned id look the same from outside

test_cases.description: Fetching a note by id without a token returns 401 before any ownership lookup
steps: GET /api/notes/<a real note id> with no Authorization header
test_cases.expected: 401 Unauthorized with error == "unauthorized"; the response body contains no note fields (no title, body, or created_at)

test_cases.description: Deleting one's own note soft-deletes it and returns the deletion timestamp
steps: POST /api/notes with a valid token and body {"body":"delete me"}; capture the id
DELETE /api/notes/<id> with the same token
test_cases.expected: 200 OK with id equal to the captured id and a non-null ISO8601 deleted_at; the MongoDB document for that id still exists (it was not removed) and now has deleted_at set to that timestamp

test_cases.description: Deleting an already-deleted note returns 404 and does not overwrite the stored deleted_at
steps: Create a note, capture the id, and DELETE /api/notes/<id>; record the returned deleted_at as T1
DELETE /api/notes/<id> a second time with the same token
Read the notes document for <id> from MongoDB
test_cases.expected: Second DELETE returns 404 with error == "not_found"; the stored deleted_at still equals T1 (unchanged by the second call) and the document count is unchanged

test_cases.description: Deleting a note that never existed returns 404 and changes no state
steps: Record the total count of documents in the notes collection
DELETE /api/notes/64b7f0000000000000000000 with a valid bearer token
DELETE /api/notes/not-an-objectid with the same token
test_cases.expected: Both calls return 404 with error == "not_found"; the notes collection document count and every existing deleted_at value are unchanged

test_cases.description: A user cannot delete another user's note
steps: As user A, POST /api/notes with body {"body":"A keeps this"}; capture idA
DELETE /api/notes/<idA> with user B's bearer token
GET /api/notes with user A's bearer token
test_cases.expected: The DELETE returns 404 (not 403); A's list still returns total == 1 including idA, and the stored document for idA still has deleted_at == null

test_cases.description: Deleting without a valid token is refused and performs no write
steps: Create a note as a user and capture its id
DELETE /api/notes/<id> with no Authorization header
DELETE /api/notes/<id> with header `Authorization: Bearer garbage`
test_cases.expected: Both calls return 401 with error == "unauthorized"; the stored note still has deleted_at == null and GET /api/notes as the owner still lists it

test_cases.description: Malformed JSON in a note-create request is rejected as 422, not 500
steps: POST /api/notes with a valid bearer token, header `Content-Type: application/json`, and a raw body of `{"body": ` (truncated, invalid JSON)
test_cases.expected: 422 Unprocessable Entity with error == "unprocessable_entity" and a details entry for field "body"; the response is never 500 and no note is created

test_cases.description: There is no update endpoint — editing is deliberately out of scope
steps: Create a note as a user and capture its id
PUT /api/notes/<id> with a valid bearer token and body {"body":"edited"}
PATCH /api/notes/<id> with the same token and body {"body":"edited"}
test_cases.expected: Both return 404 with error == "not_found" (no such endpoint); the stored note's body is still the original text and updated_at is unchanged

gaps: AS-04 (soft delete is recoverable by an operator) can only be verified by inspecting the MongoDB document directly — TC-33/TC-34 assert the surviving deleted_at, but the contract exposes no restore endpoint to test recovery end to end.

BR-07's concurrency guarantee (the unique index deciding a race between two simultaneous registrations of the same email) is not covered by a test case, because the runner issues requests sequentially; TC-02 covers only the sequential 409 path.

BR-08's timing-equivalence half (the dummy bcrypt compare making unknown-email and wrong-password indistinguishable in response time) is not asserted — TC-08 verifies only that the status and body are identical, since wall-clock timing is too noisy for a deterministic assertion.
No frontend artifacts were provided, so no UI-level tests exist for the React client described in the diagram (token storage, list rendering, compose box).
